aTickedFieldIs:
A ticked field is followed as deep as it goes, through any kind of record — this does not
                limit which record types can be pulled in, only where the search begins. The defaults are the
                fields that carry appearance. Adding others (AI packages especially) lets the search wander
                into unrelated records and copy them into the output, so tick them only if this mod needs it.

howManyLayersDeep: How many layers deep to keep searching for overridden records between finding relevant ones. This is not a total depth limit — the count resets every time a record from the mod is found, so a continuous chain of the mod's records is always followed all the way down. Default is 2, which is what lets the search cross one unrelated record (e.g. a vanilla outfit) to reach the mod's edits below it. Higher values find more obscure overrides but take exponentially longer.
howTheInProcess: How the in-process renderer sizes its decoded-texture and parsed-mesh RAM caches during mugshot generation. '% Free RAM' (default) grows the cache into a share of spare system memory; 'Fixed RAM' caps the total at the budget below; 'Disabled' turns caching off (renders decode fresh each time — slower, minimal RAM). Takes effect within a few renders; no restart needed.

ifCheckedGrabsALL: If checked, grabs ALL override records from the plugins instead of traversing from NPC records. Use with caution.

nPC2:
N.P.C.2 reads the load order from Windows' own Plugins.txt (path shown below). Mod managers such as MO2 and Vortex redirect that file to the active profile's load order, but only for programs launched through them - otherwise the Skyrim launcher's own list is used instead.

Your appearance mods are still detected, since those are read directly from the Mods folder. What breaks is everything that depends on the load order: the output plugin will not be patched against the correct conflict winners, and NPCs from anything other than the base game and Creation Club will not appear in the NPCs menu.

theNormalMapsAs: The normal maps as loaded by the Nif model don't produce maximal brightness when illuminated directly, but rather at an angle. This seems physically incorrect, since things should generally look brightest when illuminated head-on. This hack explicitly rotates non-model-space normals to maximally illuminate in the direction of the incident light, making things like eyes and hair look brighter. I think this is more accurate than default, but you can disable this if you think the generated portraits have too much glare.

vertexCountSummedAcross: Vertex count summed across all shapes.
verticalPositionThe: Vertical position the BOTTOM of the head bounding box is mapped to, expressed as a fraction of the rendered frame height (1.0 = frame top edge, 0.0 = frame bottom edge). Examples: 0.10 leaves a 10% margin below the head bottom; 0.0 puts the head bottom exactly at the frame's bottom edge; negative values (e.g. -0.1) push the head bottom below the frame for an ultra-tight crop where the chin / neck is clipped.
verticalPositionTheBOTTOM: Vertical position the BOTTOM of the head bounding box is mapped to, expressed as a fraction of the rendered frame height (1.0 = frame top edge, 0.0 = frame bottom edge). Examples: 0.10 leaves a 10% margin below the head bottom; 0.0 puts the head bottom exactly at the frame's bottom edge; negative values (e.g. -0.1) push the head bottom below the frame for an ultra-tight crop where the chin / neck is clipped. Values above the Frame Top setting are nonsensical (head bottom above head top).
verticalPositionTheTOP: Vertical position the TOP of the head bounding box is mapped to, expressed as a fraction of the rendered frame height (1.0 = frame top edge, 0.0 = frame bottom edge). Examples: 0.95 leaves a 5% margin above the head top; 1.0 puts the head top exactly at the frame's top edge; values above 1.0 push the head top above the frame for an ultra-tight crop where the top of the head is clipped.
when: When on (default), a previously-generated mugshot whose stamped metadata records missing BASE NPC assets — the NPC's own head/body/hair meshes or textures, or a FaceGen mismatch — is treated as stale and re-rendered on the next session, giving newly-installed assets a chance to fill in the wireframe / placeholder areas automatically. Turn off to keep the existing PNG in place even when it depicts an incomplete model.
whenCheckedAnInternal: When checked, an Internal-renderer mugshot whose render reports any missing meshes or textures is skipped — no PNG is written — so the batch only persists complete renders. Uncheck to save the wireframe / placeholder-textured result anyway. Per-tile clicks ignore this toggle and always render.
whenCheckedEveryInternal: When checked, every Internal-renderer load writes its full asset-resolution + renderer trace to <ExeDir>\RenderLogs\: live previews go to Preview_<ModName>_<FormKey>.txt, mugshot tile generations go to Mugshot_<ModName>_<FormKey>.txt. Use to diff a working preview against a tile that fails to render. Forces verbose logging on for the duration of the captured render.
whenCheckedThisNPC: When checked, this NPC's mugshots use the per-NPC Include Default Outfit / Include Headgear options below instead of the global Settings-tab toggles. Persists across sessions.
whenEnabledEachMugshot: When enabled, each mugshot's FaceGen NIF is parsed (or just stat'd for size-only) to surface authoring metrics. Useful for spotting absurdly heavy hair / head meshes.
whenEnabledHairAbove: When enabled, hair-above-head and other facial accessories help frame the shot - but floor-length braids are clipped at the head's lower bound so they don't blow out the frame.
whenEnabledOnlyMod: When enabled, only mod folders corresponding to enabled entries in the selected MO2 modlist.txt will be imported.
whenImportingChoicesFrom: When importing choices from your load order, winning override plugins selected here will be ignored, and the next available override will be chosen instead.
whenOn: When on (default), a mugshot is re-rendered when the settings it was generated with - lighting, camera / framing, background, resolution and render options - no longer match your current settings. Turn off to keep existing mugshots in place even after you change these settings.
whenOnA: When on, a patch run writes AssetProvenance.csv next to the .exe: one row per asset file copied into the output — which NPC, mod, and (for plugin-referenced assets) which record pulled it in, plus its source (loose or BSA). Open in a spreadsheet and sort/filter by any column. Takes effect on the next Run — no restart needed. Useful for tracing why a particular texture/mesh ended up in your output.
whenOnALoose: When on, a loose copy of an asset in your Skyrim Data folder takes precedence over the same path in any mod folder, letting your installed body / skin / texture replacers leak into mod-specific previews. FaceGen NIFs and FaceTint DDS are excluded so the mod's actual face overrides aren't replaced by vanilla copies. Off by default.
whenOnAPatch: When on, a patch run writes RecordProvenance.csv next to the .exe: one row per record merged into the output plugin (excluding the patched NPC records themselves) — its FormKey, EditorID, record type, and the full chain of references that pulled it in, from the root NPC down to the record. Open in a spreadsheet and sort/filter by any column. Takes effect on the next Run — no restart needed. Useful for tracing why a particular record ended up in your output plugin.
whenOnDefault: When on (default), a mugshot produced by an older version of the renderer (Internal) or the NPC Portrait Creator (Legacy) is treated as stale and re-rendered, so it picks up rendering fixes and improvements from the current version. Turn off to keep older-version mugshots in place.
whenOnDefaultA: When on (default), a loose copy of an asset under your Skyrim Data folder takes precedence over any BSA copy of the same path - including BSAs scoped to a non-vanilla mod. Mirrors the engine's actual rule that loose Data files override BSA-packed ones. Turn off for strict-BSA mode (preview the original mod content without your installed loose-file overrides).
whenOnDefaultAMugshot2: When on (default), a mugshot whose stamped metadata records missing outfit/headgear meshes or textures is re-rendered on the next session so newly-installed attire assets fill in the wireframe / placeholder areas. (Broken outfit physics links are excluded: nothing you install can fix a stale link inside the mod.) Turn off to keep the existing PNG in place.
whenOnDefaultAMugshot3: When on (default), a mugshot rendered with missing meshes/textures (or a detected FaceGen mismatch) shows the missing-asset warning icon, and that state is recorded in the PNG so the icon survives restarts. Unchecking hides the icon and re-renders the affected mugshots once so their recorded state is cleared. Note: while off, newly-rendered mugshots record no missing assets, so the 'Re-render When: Missing Assets' option has nothing to act on for them.
whenOnDefaultAMugshot4: When on (default), a mugshot whose outfit/headgear is missing meshes or textures — or references a physics config that doesn't exist (a broken SMP/HDT link inside the mod; the render itself is correct) — shows the outfit-assets warning icon, recorded in the PNG so it survives restarts. The missing meshes/textures re-render when you install the assets (via 'Re-render When: Missing Assets'); the broken physics link is informational. Unchecking hides the icon and re-renders the affected mugshots once so their recorded state is cleared.
whenOnRenderThe: When on, render the NPC's default outfit in mugshots and the 3D preview. Body-covering armor hides the nude body underneath. On by default.
whenOnRenderWorn: When on, render worn/outfit head gear (helmets/hoods/circlets); hair is hidden under headgear, as in game. Off by default — the sensible choice for a face-picking tool.
whenWritingTheOutput: When writing the output plugin, checks if it can be ESLified and performs the ESLification proccess
whichFieldsOfAn: Which fields of an NPC record the search for this mod's overridden records may START from.
writesAPITrafficTo: Writes API traffic to FaceFinderLog.html in the application directory (open it in any web browser). Each request is a collapsible entry with its status, headers, and full response body.
yourLoadOrderContains: Your load order contains only base game and Creation Club plugins. Relaunch N.P.C.2 through your mod manager, and check that the Skyrim Game Data Path above matches the one set in your mod manager's settings.
filterByRaceTip: Filter by race Name or EditorID. Append ~ for an exact match (e.g. NordRace~).
